speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry has any substantiated information that Singaporeans have served in the Israeli Defense Forces in 2025; (b) if yes, whether such service is in breach of our laws and whether any action will be taken; and (c) how does the Government monitor and advise citizens against being involved in foreign military conflicts.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the claims that two Singaporeans served in the Israel Defense Force will be investigated; (b) if identified, whether these individuals will be prosecuted under section 125 of the Penal Code 1871 or any other relevant legislation; and (c) whether their citizenship will be deprived should they hold dual citizenship.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs in light of reports that two Singaporeans with multiple or dual nationalities served in the Israel Defense Forces (a) how is the Ministry verifying whether any Singaporeans have served or are serving in any foreign military without authorisation; (b) if verified, what action will be taken; and (c) how will policies be reviewed to mitigate risks of unauthorised foreign military involvement by Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our loyalties as Singaporeans should only be to Singapore and we should only ever engage in military action in defence of Singapore.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have stated that and have detained people in the past for that reason.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: One is, in the event that these conflicts occur, the Minister mentioned that they do, how are the nationality obligations dealt with with the other state and what other upstream measures would the Ministry be considering to tighten the issuance of guidelines for clarity as to Singapore's stand?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Can I ask the Member to repeat her first part of the question?

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
text: I was hoping to better understand in the event that it is found that a Singaporean is involved in this case, how would Singapore be speaking with the other country in which there is involvement and what is the approach to that?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Anyone with a Singapore citizenship who is found to be engaging in a foreign armed conflict, as I have said earlier and I have said previously publicly, and my Ministry has also stated, will be dealt with in accordance with our laws.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That could include being charged and that could certainly include being detained under the Internal Security Act if they are considered to be a threat to national security.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And many have been detained on those grounds in the past and we have publicised them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If we come across credible evidence of such persons, we will normally engage with foreign counterparties to try and get such persons to Singapore, but people can appreciate, that has its own challenges.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If they are within Singapore, there is no issue; we will deal with them, as we have dealt with in the past.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the second part of the question, on how can we make it clearer, I think we have made it very clear.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The simple answer is, "Don't do it", and there is zero tolerance for it.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: First, is section 125 of the Penal Code relevant and applicable against Singapore Citizens who serve in the IDF and other foreign militaries?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: If not, what amendments are necessary to render section 125 relevant to penalise the act of serving in a foreign military?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Member said that he had two supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I assume that question comprises both questions, is it?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Well, whether section 125 applies really depends on the facts and that would require investigation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In the past, we have often used the Internal Security Act as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In our view, given the positions we have stated, the current legal framework, including the Internal Security Act, is adequate.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Would the Government be seeking clarification with the Israeli counterparts to verify the allegations as reported in the press?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And one must understand that there are obviously difficulties that other governments may face in complying with this request.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have made these sorts of requests and other sorts of requests to various governments.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Sometimes, we get answers; sometimes, we do not get answers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And persons who may be doing these things in other countries, whether in Ukraine or Russia, in the Middle East or elsewhere, or for Israel, may not be under any legal obligation to declare either their dual citizenship or any other fact relating to themselves.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And in such situations, those governments will not be able to even force them to give answers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They may well know that there are citizens or they may not even know because even their dual citizenship need not be reported.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, the Israeli government, or for that matter, the Ukrainian government or the Russian or other governments, may not even know that these people hold the dual citizenship.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And any requests would then have to be made to all their soldiers, "Let us know all your dual citizenships." And such a request is probably not enforceable.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am just sketching out to the Member the difficulties that foreign governments will have in complying with any such request.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is fairly credibly reported that a lot of American citizens fight for Israel and that is not contrary to either American law or Israeli law.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, I assume that under Israeli law, people with dual citizenship can fight for Israel.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Which means that if the Israeli government seeks to find out such information, the soldiers may not be obliged to give that information.
